A muscle fibre relaxes when its motor neuron stops firing and the nerve stimulus is removed, so acetylcholine is cleared from the neuromuscular junction. Calcium is then actively pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, which lets tropomyosin block the myosin-binding sites on actin again. The question is cut off after "when:", so I've assumed it asks for this standard textbook condition.

CONFIDENCE: 85
